# Aaron Ontoyin Yin

> AI researcher at Vela Partners (San Francisco, remote from Accra, Ghana). Applying to PhD
> programs for Fall 2027 in deep learning and reinforcement learning, and their use in
> physical systems.

Site: https://aaron-yin.com/ · Email: aarononto909@gmail.com

## Summary

Aaron Ontoyin Yin is an AI researcher drawn to the mathematics of how models learn. The
question he now wants to study is what models actually learn, and how to make that learning
reliable. His work so far has been on interpretable LLM and ML decision-making, benchmarks,
and reinforcement learning. Next he wants to work on deep learning and reinforcement learning
methods and their use where data is scarce and mistakes are costly: physical systems
(control, robotics, dynamical systems), healthcare, and other high-stakes decisions.

At Vela Partners since January 2024, he builds and maintains the research group's dataset
of tens of thousands of startups and their founders, built the founder-success prediction
models in production at the firm (precision about ten times the 1.9% base rate), and started
think-reason-learn, the group's open-source LLM-native machine-learning framework. He has
co-authored eight papers with the group and is an inventor on the GPTree patent application
(US 19/357,996). The group publishes with collaborators at the University of Oxford.

He holds a B.Sc. in Electrical & Electronic Engineering (First Class, 3.91/4.0) from the
University of Mines and Technology, Tarkwa, Ghana. He led software development for UMaT's
Drillbotics entries: a digital-twin planner for directional drilling (winner, virtual-rig
directional-drilling category, 2023) and an LSTM model that detects kicks from real-time
virtual-rig sensor data and triggers automated well control with human override, built to
connect to physical rigs through the D-WIS interface (winner, well-control category, 2024).
The work led to two SPE conference papers.
